page: Microsoft Azure E2d_v4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the EDv4 server family. It is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The CPU features hyper-threading with 2 threads per core and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It supports hardware-assisted virtualization via Microsoft Hyper-V, alongside instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 77 GB of local storage, but does not feature any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the E2d_v4 exhibits limited computational and memory throughput. Its stress-ng single-core performance is categorized in the bottom 25%, while multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also rank in the bottom 10%. However, single-threaded tasks show moderate capability, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression achieving average performance in the middle 50% tier.

Due to its low multi-core processing capacity and poor database operation benchmarks, this server is not suited for high-throughput transactional databases or parallelized compute workloads. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive but computationally light workloads, such as basic caching, lightweight web serving, or single-threaded text and image processing tasks that require a larger memory footprint than standard general-purpose instances.
